synopsis: EMESRT PR-5A Rev 3.0, dated September 2024, provides mining surface-interaction scenarios and a nine-layer control model whose Level 9 automatically slows and stops machines; intervention is only one layer, not a silver bullet [f2120, f7744, f390]. Collisions remain a practical problem: New South Wales reported no meaningful year-on-year reduction in vehicle interactions in July 2023 and recorded 30 underground collisions involving load-haul-dump machines and personnel transports in the 12 months to mid-2025 [f3003, f3004, f11446]. Validation coverage is misaligned with fatality evidence: 85% of research cases addressed vehicle–vehicle interactions, but these accounted for only 9% of the 91 fatal haul-truck accidents reviewed for 2005–2018, while vehicle–environment events accounted for the largest share [f5822, f5824]. Virtual tests therefore need multiple actors, site traffic rules and geometry, and recognition that other actors may react to braking; automatic or partial braking can itself create following-machine conflicts [f4358, f10670, f5547, f6267, f11260]. Scenario-based acceptance already covers following, overtaking, head-on encounters, junctions, multiple interactors and congested areas, while representative-mine interaction tests follow laboratory testing and a controlled mixed-traffic pilot is expected by the site operations manager [f2456, f1355, f11142]. Important uncertainties remain: no comparable large off-road naturalistic interaction dataset was found, published descriptions cite 24 PR-5A scenarios versus 17 storyboards, and one planning passage explicitly did not review EMESRT interaction controls [f6859, f7745, f9808].
